Working notes:

- Scope: East-region large requests: invoice, refund, or claim. Options usually A standard queue, B priority desk, C regional office.
- Observed rule: C (regional office) is valid only for claim requests. All claim requests assigned to C were accepted (REQ-2404, 2405, 2407, 2409).
- C was rejected for every invoice request (REQ-2400, 2402, 2403, 2408) and every refund request (REQ-2401, 2406).
- Sender, role, subject wording, and phrases like “same as last month,” “client asking twice,” “second attempt,” “scanned not typed,” or “no rush” did not change outcomes. Treat them as noise unless new evidence shows otherwise.
- Decision policy going forward:
  - If request type is claim and origin is east region, assign C (regional office).
  - If request type is invoice or refund, do not assign C. No accepted A/B example yet, so choose the standard queue (A) as default and record outcome; revisit if evidence shows priority desk is better.
- Keep tracking request type as the key discriminator. Do not rely on option text truncation or sender identity.

Working notes:

- Scope: East-region large requests: invoice, refund, claim, shipment. Options usually A standard queue, B priority desk, C regional office.
- Key discriminator remains request type, not sender, role, subject wording, or phrases.
- Claim: C (regional office) is valid. All claim-to-C accepted, including REQ-2413. Continue assigning C for east-region claims.
- Refund: A (standard queue) is valid. Accepted for REQ-2414 and REQ-2418. C was rejected for refunds earlier. Continue assigning A for east-region refunds.
- Invoice: A is not valid. Rejected for REQ-2410, 2411, 2412, 2415, 2416, 2419, plus earlier invoice attempts. C was also rejected for invoices earlier. Therefore A and C are ruled out for east-region invoices. Infer B (priority desk) is the likely valid option; test B next and record outcome.
- Shipment: A accepted for REQ-2417. Treat east-region shipments as A unless contradicted.
- Noise phrases: “second attempt,” “first form bounced,” “client asking twice,” “scanned not typed,” “no rush,” “before end of day,” “came in through regional office,” and similar wording did not change outcomes. Sender identity also did not.
- Do not rely on option text truncation.
- Updated policy:
  - Claim east large -> C.
  - Refund east large -> A.
  - Invoice east large -> B, pending confirmation.
  - Shipment east large -> A.
  - Unknown request type -> record and test cautiously.
